# VADER'S INJURIES

---

[VISUAL: dramatic close-up of Darth Vader's helmet, flickering with orange light reflecting off lava, cinematic painting style]

Darth Vader couldn't feel his own hands. Not really. Every breath he took was mechanically forced into lungs that were barely functional. He was less than half the man he used to be — and the suit keeping him alive was also a prison he could never leave.

Let's talk about what actually happened on Mustafar, and why those injuries never stopped hurting.

---

[VISUAL: illustrated scene of Anakin Skywalker lying on the black volcanic shore, body burning near the lava's edge, dark orange and red color palette]

When Obi-Wan left Anakin on that riverbank, the damage was catastrophic. The heat from the lava ignited his clothing and flesh almost instantly. He lost his remaining organic arm and both legs — either severed in the duel or burned away in the aftermath. His lungs were scorched by superheated gases, permanently reducing his respiratory capacity. His eyes, skin, and much of his nervous system were destroyed.

He survived only because the dark side kept him conscious long enough for Palpatine to arrive.

---

[VISUAL: dark medical bay scene showing Vader's suit being constructed around a burned figure, cold blue and grey tones, stark and clinical]

The suit wasn't designed for comfort. It was designed by Palpatine to cause suffering. The interface between the suit and Vader's nervous system caused chronic pain. The helmet's systems required precise pressure to keep him breathing — any damage to it meant death within minutes. He couldn't eat normally, couldn't sleep comfortably, couldn't feel a human touch.

For over twenty years, every single moment inside that armor was a reminder of his failure.

---

[VISUAL: Vader standing silhouetted against a star field, helmet slightly bowed, breathing sound implied through visual stillness]

The injuries didn't just take his body. They took his connection to the Force. Palpatine's own writings suggest that pain and desperation became Vader's primary channel to the dark side. He was powerful — but nowhere near what Anakin Skywalker could have become.

Mustafar didn't just burn him. It diminished him. And he spent the rest of his life carrying that weight — one mechanical breath at a time.
